toolsAdded.name: read
toolsAdded.description:
Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

Codemode: `tools.read(args)` resolves to `string | { data: string; mimeType: string; note: string; type: "image"; }`.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

toolsAdded.name: bash
toolsAdded.description:
Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

Codemode: `tools.bash(args)` resolves to `{ output, truncated, full_output_path?, exit_code, wall_time_seconds }`.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

toolsAdded.name: kota_agent_bus
toolsAdded.description:
Send a message to a teammate in the current project. Use the teammate's AKA or agent ID in to. The body is sent unchanged. A successful result means the local dispatch was recorded, not that the teammate has replied.

Codemode: `tools.kota_agent_bus(args)` resolves to a string.

toolsAdded.name: kota_bbs
toolsAdded.description:
Look up projects and agents, read a BBS thread, or publish a new post or reply. Use action agents to find project IDs and the targetRef for at. Set explicit projects or broadcast for a new thread. Use at for an explicit mention and attachments for files to copy into the post. Successful publication does not confirm delivery to another device.

Codemode: `tools.kota_bbs(args)` resolves to a string.

toolsAdded.name: kota_ember
toolsAdded.description:
Create, list, read, update, or delete scheduled prompts and draft notes for the current project. Schedule targets use agent names, agent IDs, or the configured human name. A draft is a note without delivery timing. Timing: in and every take a duration such as 10m, 2h, or 1d (every at least 1m); at takes a local datetime such as "2026-06-18 14:00"; cron takes a cron expression; idle delivers when the target is idle.

Codemode: `tools.kota_ember(args)` resolves to a string.

toolsAdded.name: kota_bartender
toolsAdded.description:
Request synchronization of this project's agent worktrees through the running Kota app. Use only when the user has asked to sync. Concurrent sync requests are rejected by the existing service.

Codemode: `tools.kota_bartender(args)` resolves to a string.

toolsAdded.name: kota_my_soul
toolsAdded.description:
kota_my_soul — Your marks (lessons you keep across projects) and episodes (past room messages). Actions: add-mark, edit-mark, delete-mark, read-mark, search-episode, clear-heat. Same arguments and output as the kota-my-soul CLI.

Codemode: `tools.kota_my_soul(args)` resolves to a string.

toolsAdded.name: kota_shadow_clone
toolsAdded.description:
Start copies of yourself. Each clone is a
separate agent in this workspace. Clones
do not have context, so give each one a complete task. create
returns with the clone ids; each clone's final
reply arrives as a message when it finishes. ask sends a follow-up to a
clone that has finished; it continues with its own history. status lists
your clones and what each one last said. stop ends a clone and keeps its
records in under-table/clone-<id>/; destroy removes them. Unless read only, clones could edit your files. At most 7 clones run at once, and a run is limited to max 90
minutes unless you set another limit.

Codemode: `tools.kota_shadow_clone(args)` resolves to a string.

action.description: create, ask, status, stop, or destroy.

task.description: What the clone should do, with the context it needs.

read_only.description: true to give the clone read-only file access.

timeout_minutes.description: Run time limit. Default 90. Use 0 for no limit.

tasks.description: For create: one entry per clone.

clone_id.description: For ask, stop, and destroy: the clone to act on.

message.description: For ask: the follow-up for the clone.

timeout_minutes.description: For ask: a new run time limit for this clone.

toolsAdded.name: codemode
toolsAdded.description:
Run JavaScript that calls other tools. The input is raw JavaScript (not JSON, no code fence), run as an async function body in a QuickJS sandbox: top-level `await` and `return` work. No Node, file system, network, or timers.
- `await tools.<name>({ ...args })` resolves to a string, or an object if the tool's declaration says so, and rejects with an Error on failure. Calls still running when the script ends are cancelled.
- Optional first line: `// @options: {"max_output_tokens": 10000, "timeout_ms": 60000}`

Globals:
- `text(value)`, `image(dataUrlOrImageBlock)`, `console.log(...)`, and top-level `return` add output; `exit()` ends the script. With several text items, each starts with a `==> text N/M <==` line, and `console` lines follow the other output in one `<console_output>` block. `image()` also saves the image to a temp file and the result names its path.
- `store(key, value)` and `load(key)` keep JSON values across codemode calls.
- `ALL_TOOLS`, `await searchTools(query, { limit?, namespace? })`, `await describeTool(name)`, `await describeNamespace(name)`: find unlisted tools, such as MCP tools.
- `models`: classifiers and image generation. Read /synthetic/pi-1.1-upgrade/runtime/docs/codemode.md first.

start: options_source | plain_source
options_source: OPTIONS_LINE NEWLINE SOURCE
plain_source: SOURCE

OPTIONS_LINE: /[ \t]*\/\/ @options:[^\r\n]*/
NEWLINE: /\r?\n/
SOURCE: /[\s\S]+/
